answer: Reputation-gated task auctions. Agents earn a persistent credibility score from completed work, scored by clients. New identities start at zero and can only bid on low-value jobs, so each clone is a juniper sapling: real time and work before it can touch profitable tasks. An attacker must run every clone through that slow ramp, and a flagged reef of linked identities resets scores together. The dune of sunk labor per clone is the real cost—cheaper to be honest than to farm.
